title: Design Helix: Contribution Lifecycle & Sunset Framework
creator: Asha Patel
description: Establish a single, developer-friendly lifecycle for design system contributions and a clear, low-friction sunset path for tokens and components. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc decisions, accelerate safe changes, and create predictable migration paths for product teams.
problem_statement: Multiple teams modify tokens and UI primitives using different review patterns and implicit assumptions. This has led to inconsistent token naming, stale accessibility checks on components, and last-minute rollbacks when production behavior changes. We need a formal, lightweight governance model that scales with contributors while minimizing friction for small, safe edits.
goals: 1) Create a contribution lifecycle that defines tiers of change (minor edit, feature component, breaking change) with corresponding review gates and signoffs. 2) Define a deprecation/sunset framework with timelines, migration templates, and notification rules. 3) Provide an RFC cadence and template for larger design decisions tied to engineering rollout plans.
scope_included: Token changes, button/table/chart components, visual primitives, design docs and component API surface changes.
scope_excluded: App-specific feature UI that does not publish to the shared library and infra-level runtime optimizations handled by Engineering tickets.
proposal_summary: Introduce 'Design Helix' — a three-tier change classification and review checklist. Tier A: cosmetic or token tweaks that can be merged with single design reviewer approval and automated accessibility smoke tests. Tier B: component behavior/API changes requiring design + eng review and an RFC for non-trivial surface changes. Tier C: breaking changes or removals requiring RFC, migration plan, two-week notice, and a deprecation branch to preserve backward compatibility during rollout.
contributor_checklist: Create a short PR description with: intent, visual diff screenshots, and API diff (if any)
Reference an RFC when changing public component APIs or tokens used by >3 products
Run Storybook snapshots and local accessibility checks before requesting review
Add migration notes if keys or props are renamed
Pick the appropriate change tier in PR labels: Tier-A | Tier-B | Tier-C
review_checklist: Design reviewer: verify visual parity, token usage, and UX rationale
Engineering reviewer: check API compatibility, performance, and unit tests
Accessibility reviewer: confirm keyboard/aria behaviors and color contrast where applicable
QA reviewer or automation: validate Storybook snapshots and end-to-end smoke tests
Documentation: ensure updated tokens reference and example usage in the docs site
RFC_process: RFCs should be created for Tier-B (major surface changes) and Tier-C (breaking) proposals. RFC template: problem statement, alternatives considered, migration strategy, rollout plan, and initial acceptance criteria. RFCs go through a 10-business-day review period; urgent RFCs can be fast-tracked with lead approvals. Attach a follow-up implementation ticket referencing the RFC key.
deprecation_policy_summary: When a token or component is identified for removal, mark as deprecated in the docs and code with a deprecation banner and automated codemod suggestions. Timeline: Deprecation announcement (week 0), opt-out compatibility builds for 8 weeks, codemod availability by week 2, removal targeted at week 12 (configurable per case). Notify affected product teams via Slack channel, weekly digest, and Design System newsletter.
migration_templates: Token rename template: before/after mapping, code sample replacement commands, and Storybook diff guidance
Prop migration template: new prop usage, adapter shim example, deprecation warnings in console
Chart upgrade template: data shape diffs and preview harness link
rollout_and_communication: Create a deprecation issue with checklist and assign product owners for affected teams
Schedule a 30-minute sync with key integrators for Tier-C changes
Publish RFC and deprecation notes to Confluence and the #design-system Slack channel
Add Slack digest entry and a mention in the biweekly design-system newsletter
metrics: Number of migration help requests per deprecation
Average time from PR opened to merge by tier
Number of rollbacks or hotfixes attributed to design system changes
Docs page views for any deprecated item and codemod downloads

decisions: Adopt three-tier change classification (A/B/C) for all design-system PRs
Require RFCs for Tier-B & Tier-C changes with a 10-business-day review by default
Standardize 12-week maximum removal window for deprecations unless a shorter window is agreed with product owners
